cases.name: sample_by_fixed
cases.query_origin: Hand-written QuestDB SQL regression from the developer dashboard
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_datetime AS time, count() AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' SAMPLE BY 5m
cases.rationale: Fixed five-minute SAMPLE BY buckets are aligned to the epoch grid and can be merged by the native delta cache.

cases.name: sample_by_series
cases.query_origin: Hand-written QuestDB SQL regression from the developer dashboard
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_datetime AS time, cab_type, count() AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' SAMPLE BY 15m
cases.rationale: QuestDB groups every plain non-time select column into the series identity when SAMPLE BY has no explicit GROUP BY.

cases.name: sample_by_fill_null
cases.query_origin: Hand-written QuestDB SQL regression from the developer dashboard
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_datetime AS time, avg(total_amount) AS value FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' SAMPLE BY 10m FILL(NULL) ORDER BY time
cases.rationale: NULL fill preserves the absence of a bucket and is safe to restore around the rendered extent.

cases.name: timestamp_floor
cases.query_origin: Hand-written QuestDB SQL regression from the developer dashboard
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT timestamp_floor('5m', pickup_datetime) AS time, count() AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: QuestDB's fixed-width timestamp_floor expression exposes the same reusable time axis as SAMPLE BY.

cases.name: epoch_floor
cases.query_origin: Hand-written QuestDB SQL regression for PostgreSQL-compatible epoch bucketing
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT floor(extract(epoch FROM pickup_datetime)/300)*300 AS time, count() AS trips FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.rationale: The shared epoch-floor matcher is retained for clients that express QuestDB-compatible buckets in PostgreSQL-style SQL.

cases.name: object_month_sample
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_datetime AS time, count() FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' SAMPLE BY 1M
cases.rationale: Calendar months are not a fixed duration and therefore cannot use the fixed-width delta cache.

cases.name: object_fill_prev
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_datetime AS time, count() FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' SAMPLE BY 5m FILL(PREV)
cases.rationale: Previous-value fill depends on neighboring rows outside an independently fetched extent, so it remains an object response.

cases.name: object_from_to_sample
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_datetime AS time, count() FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' SAMPLE BY 5m FROM '2026-09-18T08:00:00Z' TO '2026-09-18T11:00:00Z' FILL(NULL)
cases.rationale: QuestDB's SAMPLE BY FROM/TO clause owns the sampling bounds and cannot be replaced by a cache extent.

cases.name: object_explicit_group
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT pickup_datetime AS time, cab_type, count() FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' GROUP BY cab_type SAMPLE BY 5m
cases.rationale: The analyzer does not guess how an explicit GROUP BY combines with QuestDB's implicit SAMPLE BY grouping.

cases.name: object_timestamp_not_first
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT cab_type, pickup_datetime AS time, count() FROM trips WHERE pickup_datetime >= '2026-09-18T08:00:03.123456Z' AND pickup_datetime < '2026-09-18T11:00:07.456789Z' SAMPLE BY 5m
cases.rationale: QuestDB applies SAMPLE BY to the designated timestamp; the adapter only infers the first plain selected column and otherwise fails closed.
